signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers JPY as the weekly leader up +1.231% across 7 pairs, while SEK anchors as the laggard down -1.507% across 2 pairs. This generates an extreme leader-to-laggard bilateral spread of 2.738%, surpassing the threshold for a strong thematic move. JPY strength accelerates despite an accommodative real policy rate of -1.70% and a 266bp OIS carry disadvantage against USD, supported instead by an economic surprise index of +23.8. Conversely, the Riksbank holds policy at 1.75% against a negative SEK ESI of -6.7, leaving the krona defenseless across crosses. Speculative JPY positioning remains heavily stretched short with Leveraged Funds holding net -111,297 contracts (2nd percentile of 52-week range, z=-2.18), creating asymmetric short-covering fuel. Trade bias: Long JPY/SEK; bilateral performance spread reflects structural divergence and spec short squeeze risk. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Swedish inflation metrics rebound sharply, triggering a hawkish repricing in Riksbank forward curves.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Bear Steepener + Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.48, holding below its daily SMA20 at 157.91, SMA50 at 159.85, and SMA200 at 158.42. The US Treasury curve displays a bear steepener with 2s10s expanding to +51.4bp as US 10Y yields push to 4.944% following surging crude oil past $104. Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% provides an active +275bp policy spread, reinforced by a +266bp SOFR-TONA carry advantage that fundamentally favors USD. However, 25-delta risk reversals print an extreme put skew of -2.04 vols, indicating aggressive institutional bidding for downside protection despite retail sentiment sitting at 86% long. The options market is aggressively positioning for spot downside while Leveraged Funds sit deeply short JPY at -111,297 contracts (WoW -29,678), creating acute squeeze vulnerability. Trade bias: Short USD/JPY; severe options downside hedging and spec short crowding override nominal carry. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Core CPI prints above 0.3% m/m, driving US 10Y yields above 5.05% and re-establishing carry dominance.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Sentiment Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7159, hovering directly below its SMA20 at 0.7164 while maintaining an posture above the SMA50 at 0.7065 and SMA200 at 0.7001. CFTC data shows institutional Leveraged Funds net long AUD by +50,250 contracts, sitting at the 94th percentile of its 52-week distribution (z=+1.79), yet weekly flows stalled with a net reduction of -3,328 contracts. Simultaneously, Myfxbook retail sentiment registers an extreme 91% short positioning against institutional longs, establishing a clean speculative divergence. The RBA cash rate at 4.35% yields a 60bp nominal premium over the Fed's 3.75% (AONIA-SOFR spread of -71bp favoring AUD), but Australia's real policy rate remains mildly accommodative at -0.55% due to 4.90% inflation expectations. While retail short capitulation risks provide upside convexity, the stalling institutional buying limits further extension into resistance. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional positioning dominance and retail short squeeze setup. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US CPI surprise accelerates the bear steepener in US yields, triggering leveraged liquidation of AUD longs below 0.7065.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Rates Spread + Technical SMA Resistance
signals.text: EUR/USD prints at 1.1613, capped beneath the converging SMA20 at 1.1629 and SMA200 at 1.1637, while remaining above its SMA50 at 1.1529. Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.5% maintains a 125bp policy rate advantage in favor of the dollar, translating to a +145bp SOFR vs €STR CIP carry spread that structurally caps euro upside. ECB holds at 2.5%. Leveraged Funds positioning reflects this differential with EUR net short at -52,784 contracts, though modest weekly short-covering of +2,527 contracts aligns with options market neutrality as 25-delta risk reversals sit flat at -0.06. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent 145bp OIS carry drag and moving-average overhead cluster limit upside momentum. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech today at 08:00 UTC followed by US CPI at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Lagarde delivers an explicitly hawkish forward commitment that drives 10Y Bund yields higher, forcing a close above 1.1640.
